title: dhammānupassī
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en:
“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dwell observing phenomena as phenomena?
Here a bhikkhu dwells observing phenomena as phenomena in regard to the five hindrances.
And how does a bhikkhu dwell observing phenomena as phenomena in regard to the five hindrances?

and he also understands how there comes to be the arising of unarisen sensual desire, and how there comes to be the abandoning of arisen sensual desire, and how there comes to be the future non-arising of abandoned sensual desire.
… He understands: ‘There is ill-will in me’ …
He understands: ‘There is dullness and drowsiness in me’ …
He understands: ‘There is restlessness and remorse in me’ …

There being doubt in him, a bhikkhu understands:
‘There is doubt in me’; or there being no doubt in him,
he understands: ‘There is no doubt in me’;
and he understands how there comes to be the arising of unarisen doubt, and how there comes to be the abandoning of arisen doubt,
and how there comes to be the future non-arising of abandoned doubt.

In this way he dwells observing phenomena as phenomena internally, or he dwells observing phenomena as phenomena externally, or he dwells observing phenomena as phenomena both internally and externally.
Or he dwells observing in phenomena their nature of arising, or he dwells observing in phenomena their nature of vanishing, or he dwells observing in phenomena their nature of both arising and vanishing.

Or else awareness that ‘there are phenomena’
is simply established in him to the extent necessary for bare knowledge and awareness. And he abides independent, not clinging to anything in the world.
That is how a bhikkhu dwells observing phenomena as phenomena in regard to the five hindrances.”
